rationale: A wins because it is tougher about what a reporter can actually verify; "A Calm-funded trial reports an 18% drop in anxiety - the question is whether \"regular users\" is doing the heavy lifting" is the cleanest editorial instinct in either set. B is still useful, but "Calm built 4 million paying subscribers. Its next 25 million users won't pay it directly" turns covered members into users, which is exactly the kind of denominator slippage that gets a pitch punished. The margin is slight because B's member-utilization angle is real; A is just more disciplined about proof and the next step.
gaps_in_A: "Wellness apps are crossing from app-store impulse buy into reimbursed health benefit" states a trend from one supplied deal; A correctly asks for comparables, but the headline should carry that caveat until they exist.
"who tracks how consumer subscription apps survive once growth slows" smuggles in a growth-slowdown premise not present in the update.
"AI-slop/sponsored-research skepticism journalists are writing about right now" is an external zeitgeist claim without supplied evidence; unnecessary decoration on an otherwise sharp proof critique.
It misses a clean member-benefit utilization angle: 25 million covered members plus the "regular users" caveat creates a people-affected story, not only payer/category and methodology stories.
gaps_in_B: "Its next 25 million users won't pay it directly" is factually loose. The update says 25 million covered members, not 25 million users.
"category-creation" is startup-conference perfume. One covered-benefit deal can support a coverage-line story; it does not prove a category was created.
"Next step: journalist-fit-check" is premature. Before reporter matching, Calm needs insurer names, journal citation, study methods, and any disclosable economics.

"A meditation app becomes a covered insurance benefit for 25 million members" is good, but B does not demand comparable payer examples or evidentiary-bar context, so the category angle risks staying a single-company announcement.
